messages:
meera: Heads-up — HarborBridge POC wants to onboard a custom model variant into our catalog for a Dedicated + Private (VPC) deployment. They claim it's a Llama2-derivative 13B quantized to int4. Key asks: compatibility with Private, KMS requirements, and a reserved-capacity pricing ballpark. Any immediate red flags?

youssef: @meera need to know artifact format first (HF repo or TorchScript), tokenizer compatibility, and whether architecture changes (e.g., added adapters). Also: expected max sequence length and KV cache behaviour — that drives memory.

meera: They provided a repo: https://git.example.com/harborbridge/harbor-bridge-v2 (internal link). Readme says HF format, tokenizer is SentencePiece, max_seq_len 2048, heavy KV caching for retrieval-augmented generation.

samir: int4 on customer kernels can be tricky. For stable int4 execution we recommend Nvidia G5/RTX6000Ada or the new H100-era kernels; older Ampere may need custom ops. Quick action: run our compatibility check.

samir: Try `rictl model-check --repo https://git.example.com/harborbridge/harbor-bridge-v2 --targets private,dedicated --output json` — it reports required memory, supported runtimes, and any missing ops.

youssef: Also they must include a model manifest in the repo. Minimal fields: `architecture`, `weight_format`, `quantization`, `tokenizer`, `sample_input`. If missing, our onboarding will stall.

meera: Noted. I asked them to add manifest and sample inputs.

linda: For Private/VPC we need KMS key flow documented and confirmation they won't process regulated data by default. Also request the completed security questionnaire (we have a template). If customer expects HSM integration, escalate to Enterprise sales.

meera: I'll push the questionnaire to them today. Any pricing guidance for a short trial then monthly reserved? They asked for a 3-month POC then decide on 4x reserved GPUs.

samir: For a 13B int4 variant with heavy KV caching, assume 1x instance type G5-32/40GB or 1x A100-80GB for stable perf. For dedicated throughput, 4 GPUs reserved is reasonable for their qps. For numbers: engineering estimate = baseline node cost + 20% overhead for autoscaling. I'll give a concrete SKU cost after the model-check run.

meera: Good. I'll tell them ballpark and that we'll firm numbers after the scan.

samir: Also recommend they publish an int8 fallback variant. int4 can be brittle; fallback to int8 avoids outage if we need to route to lower tiers. We can stage rollouts: canary -> A/B -> global.

meera: Can we automate a variant compatibility scan and produce a short report to share with customer?

samir: Yes: `rictl variant-scan --model harbor-bridge-v2 --variants int4,int8 --report /tmp/hb-scan.json` then `rictl summarize-report /tmp/hb-scan.json` — returns runtimes, kernel gaps, estimated memory per-token, and recommended GPU families. I'll run it once manifest is added.

deploy-bot: model-scan queued (job id: 983102) — will notify when finished. :gear:

linda: Also flagging legal: if they need dedicated private deployment we need an addendum for key custody + SOC2 controls. Sales should loop Legal early.

meera: Action items: 1) @youssef — review manifest and run the variant-scan when ready. 2) @samir — confirm recommended GPU SKUs & provide cost stub. 3) @linda — send security questionnaire and checklist to HarborBridge. I'll coordinate next steps with the AE and loop Legal if they request HSM.

meera: Thanks all — I'll update thread with the repo manifest link and the scan output once available.
